question.text: What will India's total meat production per capita be during 2026-2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the total meat production per capita of India during 2026-27 as reported by [the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying](https://www.dahd.gov.in/) of the Government of India.

research:
As of 2026-11-19, the official figure the question resolves on (per capita meat for 2026-27) has not been published, and it won't be until about November 2027. The latest official value is **7.51 kg per year for 2024-25**. The 2025-26 figure should come out with BAHS 2026, probably around National Milk Day, 2026-11-26.

## 1. Resolution source
- The figure will come from the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics (BAHS) report published by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), part of the Ministry. The 2026-27 numbers should appear in BAHS 2027. That report is based on the Integrated Sample Survey (ISS), which runs from 1 March to the end of February in three seasons, so it covers March 2026 to February 2027.
- 2025-11-26 (National Milk Day): DAHD released BAHS 2025, covering 2024-25. Total meat output was 10.50 million tonnes, up 2.46% on 10.25 Mt in 2023-24. Poultry made up 5.18 Mt, about half. [PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2195049&reg=3&lang=2)
- 2026-02: The full BAHS 2025 report table gives per capita meat as **7.51 kg/annum for 2024-25, up from 7.39 in 2023-24 (+1.62%)**. The report's text, quoted in the question background, says 7.50, so rounding differs within the same report. [DAHD release PDF](https://www.dahd.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/02/1bb7d351f8d648f0228025825769c7e0.pdf), [BAHS2025](https://dahd.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-02/BAHS2025.pdf)
- I couldn't read the DAHD statistics page: it returned a 404, and the site is built by scripts. I found no CSV or API behind it, and there is no higher-frequency official series that leads this figure.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The 2025-26 figure, which is the step before the one asked about, isn't out. I found no published 2025-26 meat estimate as of 2026-11-19.
- Timing risk: the BAHS 2025 brochure came out in November 2025, but the full report only appeared in February 2026. If BAHS 2027 is late, the figure may not be out by the resolution date of about 2027-11-30.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-17: The third advance horticulture estimates for 2025-26 were 386.9 Mt (+4.36%). This is a different ministry and not a meat figure, but it shows these annual releases are on schedule. [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/record-horticultural-production-shows-increase-of-436-from-2024-25-agriculture-ministry/article71712523.ece)
- 2026 (date not given): ICRA expects organised poultry earnings to improve in FY27 as broiler prices recover. It says recent bird flu outbreaks have been "localised and temporary". [Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/icra-sees-poultry-earnings-improving-as-broiler-prices-recover-in-fy27)
- 2026-02 to 2026-03: There were H5N1 culls in Patna (about 6,000 birds) and Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh. A March headline reported chicken prices soaring on bird deaths and lower bird weights. [Lokmat](https://www.lokmattimes.com/national/bird-flu-6000-chickens-culled-in-patna/amp), [Pulse](https://www.pulse.bot/commodities/news/chicken-prices-soar-in-india-on-bird-mortality-reduced-weight-d683fcb8-7d21-446e-a141-e084ad338952)
- 2025-12: The head of Poultry India said broiler production is growing 6-7% a year. This is an industry estimate, not official data. [S&P Global](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/agriculture/122925-interview-indias-broiler-production-continues-to-expand-6-7-annually-says-poultry-india-head)
- 2025-12: Kerala reported 11 H5N1 outbreaks on farms to WOAH, the World Organisation for Animal Health. I only have this from search summaries and did not open the report.

## 4. Base rates (per capita meat, kg/annum, official BAHS unless noted)

| Year | kg/annum | Change | Total meat (Mt) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2018-19 | 6.15 | | 8.11 |
| 2019-20 | 6.45 (secondary source) | +0.30 | |
| 2020-21 | 6.52 (Invest India) | +0.07 (COVID year) | |
| 2021-22 | 6.82 | +0.30 | |
| 2022-23 | 7.10 | +0.28 | |
| 2023-24 | 7.39 | +0.29 | 10.25 |
| 2024-25 | 7.51 | +0.12 | 10.50 (+2.46%) |

- Sources: [Factly](https://factly.in/meat-production-rises-29-in-india-but-five-states-drive-most-of-the-supply/), [DAHD MLP growth](https://dahd.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-10/MlpGrowthRate202223.pdf), [UpdatedCompendium2022-23](https://dahd.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-10/UpdatedCompendium2022-23.pdf)
- The per capita figure has risen every year since 2018-19. Yearly gains ranged from +0.07 to +0.30 kg, and the median was about +0.29.
- Growth slowed in the latest year: total output grew only 2.46%, against roughly 5% a year before that.
- The question needs two more yearly steps from 7.51. That is simple arithmetic, not a forecast:
  - two steps at the low end (+0.07 to +0.12 a year) give about 7.65 to 7.75;
  - two steps at the typical size (+0.28 to +0.30) give about 8.07 to 8.11.
- The per capita figure divides output by DAHD's population estimates (I couldn't check which projection they use). If those population figures are revised, the ratio moves too.
- Seasonality: this is an annual survey covering March to February, so there's no within-year pattern that matters here.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market, Metaculus question or expert forecast on India's per capita meat output. None of the markets provided match this question: they cover US oil, Arkansas broilers, Nebraska corn and others.
- The only outside indicators are industry growth claims (broilers +6-7% a year) and ICRA's poultry outlook for FY27.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-11-26: BAHS 2026 is likely to give the 2025-26 meat output and per capita figure. This is the most important next data point.
- March 2026 to February 2027: the ISS survey seasons that produce the 2026-27 estimate.
- Bird flu outbreaks in winter 2026-27 could hit poultry, which is about half of all meat.
- About 2027-11-26: BAHS 2027, which should resolve the question. A brochure may come before the full report, as happened in 2025.
- Weather matters only indirectly, through feed costs. I didn't look up any monsoon outlook because the link to meat output is weak.

Other sources: [DAHD BAHS 2025 (June upload)](https://www.dahd.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/06/9ae804b82e59e283443396dbb5a245e0.pdf), [PIB National Milk Day 2025](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/nov/doc20251125706201.pdf)

I found nothing that settles this yet. The 2026-27 figure won't be published until about November 2027. India's ministry (DAHD) has not yet put out the 2025-26 number. Most pages on dahd.gov.in, pib.gov.in and factly.in blocked me (HTTP 403), and the statistics landing page in the question returns a 404. So several figures below come from secondary summaries.

## 1. Resolution source
- The figure that decides this is the per capita meat availability line (kg/annum) in DAHD's Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics (BAHS). The 2026-27 value should appear in BAHS 2027, likely around November 2027.
- 2025-11 (released around National Milk Day, Nov 26; full PDF on the site 2026-02): BAHS 2025 says meat production was 10.25 MT in 2023-24 and 10.50 MT in 2024-25 (+2.46%). Per capita availability went from 6.15 kg/annum in 2018-19 to **7.50 kg/annum in 2024-25**, the latest official value. [BAHS2025 release](https://www.dahd.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/02/1bb7d351f8d648f0228025825769c7e0.pdf); [Vet Extension summary](https://www.vetextension.com/livestock-production-statistics-of-india-2025/)
- 2026-06: DAHD posted a BAHS PDF, but by search summaries its meat tables still stop at 2024-25. [DAHD PDF](https://www.dahd.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/06/9ae804b82e59e283443396dbb5a245e0.pdf)
- Implied population: 10.50 MT ÷ 7.50 kg ≈ 1.40 billion. This is my own arithmetic, not a stated figure.
- There is no higher-frequency official series. The estimate comes from the annual Integrated Sample Survey, which runs March to February. For 2026-27 that is March 2026 to February 2027.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled. The 2026-27 survey year is still running until February 2027.
- 2026-11-19: I found no BAHS 2026 (the 2025-26 figure) yet. Past reports came out on November 26, so it is probably due in about a week.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-11-17: The third advance estimates put 2025-26 horticulture output at a record 386.9 MT (+4.36%). This is crops, not livestock, but it shows the ministries publishing their annual numbers on schedule. [The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/record-horticultural-production-shows-increase-of-436-from-2024-25-agriculture-ministry/article71712523.ece)
- 2025 (USDA attaché report): USDA projects Indian carabeef (buffalo meat) output at 4.7 MMT in 2026, up from 4.6 MMT in 2025. [USDA GAIN IN2025-0048](https://apps.fas.usda.gov/newgainapi/api/Report/DownloadReportByFileName?fileName=Livestock+and+Products+Annual_New+Delhi_India_IN2025-0048.pdf)
- 2024-11-26: BAHS 2024 put 2023-24 meat output at 10.25 MT (+4.95%). [Drishti IAS](https://www.drishtiias.com/daily-updates/daily-news-analysis/basic-animal-husbandry-statistics-2024)
- I found no 2026 news on bird flu or poultry shocks. My search only turned up stories from 2006-2021.

## 4. Base rates
Official per capita series (kg/annum), from BAHS releases and summaries ([pashudhanpraharee](https://pashudhanpraharee.com/?p=31279), [DAHD BAHS2023](https://dahd.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/BAHS2023.pdf)):

| Year | Per capita (kg) | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2018-19 | 6.15 | |
| 2019-20 | 6.45 | +0.30 |
| 2020-21 | 6.52 | +0.07 (COVID) |
| 2021-22 | 6.82 | +0.30 |
| 2022-23 | 7.10 | +0.28 |
| 2023-24 | not found | the 2022-23 to 2024-25 gap is +0.40 over two years, about +0.20 a year |
| 2024-25 | 7.50 | |

- Production growth: about 5% in 2022-23 and 2023-24, then a slowdown to 2.46% in 2024-25.
- The per capita change has been positive every year since 2018-19. It averages about +0.22 kg a year, with a range of +0.07 to +0.30.
- My own extrapolation, not a forecast: at +0.07 to +0.30 a year, two years on from 7.50 gives about 7.64 to 8.10 for 2026-27.
- Caution: some figures get revised between reports. Different releases give different growth rates for the same year (for example, 4.95% vs 2.46% around 2023-24), and population projections are updated over time.
- Seasonality doesn't apply here. This is one annual survey estimate, so there is no within-year path to compare.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast for India's per capita meat production. None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets match: they cover US oil, US broilers, US corn and Indian politics.
- The only related number is USDA's 2026 carabeef projection of 4.7 MMT (+2%), above.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around 2026-11-26 (National Milk Day): BAHS 2026 is expected with the 2025-26 meat and per capita figures. This is the most informative near-term data point.
- 2027-02-28: the 2026-27 survey period ends.
- February 2027: the Census population count. If DAHD switches denominators to Census-based numbers, the per capita value could move regardless of production.
- Possible disease shocks (bird flu, foot-and-mouth disease) during 2026-27. Poultry is about half of output: 5.18 MT in 2024-25.
- Around 2027-11-26: BAHS 2027 is expected with the 2026-27 value that decides the question. Forecasts close earlier, on 2027-06-30.
- Weather is not a main driver, so I didn't pull a seasonal outlook.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About one year. BAHS 2027, which will carry the 2026-27 figure, is expected around late November 2027. A delayed full report, as happened in 2025-26, could push publication into 2028.

(b) The latest official value is 7.51 kg/annum for 2024-25, from the BAHS 2025 table published February 2026. The report's text rounds it to 7.50. The 2025-26 figure is expected around 2026-11-26.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be about 7.5 kg per capita.

(d) If the trend continued:
- At the latest slower pace (meat output +2.5% a year, per capita about +1.6% a year), the result is about 7.75.
- At the 2021-24 pace (+0.29 kg a year), the result is about 8.1.
- A blended central estimate is about 7.8 to 7.85.

(e) Annual changes since 2018-19 ranged from +0.07 to +0.30 kg. Over two steps, that gives a plausible range of +0.14 to +0.60 kg. Revisions to population estimates or the livestock-census base can add more noise.

(f) No markets or formal forecasts exist. Industry sources expect broiler production to grow 6-7% a year, and ICRA expects poultry to recover in FY27. Both modestly support the trend continuing.

(g) Scenarios:
- **Low:** A severe bird flu wave in 2026-27, combined with feed-cost stress and a methodology or population rebasing after the 21st Livestock Census, leaves per capita flat or slightly down (about 7.3 to 7.5).
- **High:** Strong poultry expansion of 7-8% a year, plus an upward re-estimation of slaughter numbers in the new census-based ISS frame, pushes it to about 8.3 to 8.5.

(a) **Time left:** The 2026-27 figure should appear in BAHS 2027, around 26 November 2027, which is about 12 months away. The full report may come later, as happened in 2025-26 when it appeared in February. The 2025-26 figure, the intermediate step, is due around 26 November 2026.

(b) **Latest known value:** 7.51 kg/annum for 2024-25, from the BAHS 2025 tables published in February 2026. The report text rounds this to 7.50. Total output was 10.50 Mt, up 2.46%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 7.5 kg.

(d) **If the trend continued:**
- Population grows about 0.9% a year.
- At the recent slower output growth of about 2.5% a year, per capita rises about 1.6% a year, giving about 7.75.
- At the longer-run output growth of about 4-5% a year, per capita gains about 0.28 kg a year, giving about 8.05 to 8.1.
- A blend centred on output growth of about 3.5% a year gives about 7.85 to 7.9.

(e) **Historical variation:** Annual gains since 2018-19 ranged from +0.07 kg (the COVID year) to +0.30 kg. Two-year changes have ranged from about +0.37 to +0.60 kg. The series has risen every year.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There are no markets or forecasts on this quantity. Industry says broiler output is growing 6-7% a year, and ICRA expects poultry earnings to recover in FY27. Both point modestly upward. The localised H5N1 outbreaks in early 2026 pull slightly down.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low: severe, widespread avian influenza in 2026-27 combined with feed-cost spikes cuts poultry output. Alternatively, a revision to the survey or population base flattens the figure, leaving it at about 7.3 to 7.5.
- High: strong poultry expansion plus a methodology change, or a downward revision to population estimates, pushes the figure to about 8.3 to 8.5.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
